possible_explanations: Revenue growth is being driven by credit sales rather than cash sales
Customer collection terms have been extended
Collection efficiency has declined relative to sales growth
evidence_to_check: Notes to accounts — trade receivables ageing schedule
MD&A — commentary on credit policy or customer terms
investigation_path: Compare receivables growth rate to revenue growth rate
Review receivables ageing schedule for signs of slower collection
Check MD&A for any stated change in credit or collection policy

possible_explanations: Revenue recognized is not yet converting to cash, indicating working-capital build-up
Collection cycle has lengthened, delaying cash realization
evidence_to_check: Cash flow statement — working capital adjustments line
investigation_path: Quantify the gap between revenue growth and CFO growth
Check whether receivables growth alone explains the CFO decline
Flag for analyst verification against annual report disclosures

possible_explanations: Revenue growth is being achieved at the cost of pricing or margin discipline
Cost base is growing faster than revenue
Product/segment mix has shifted toward lower-margin offerings
evidence_to_check: MD&A — commentary on pricing, discounts, or cost pressures
investigation_path: Break down margin change by cost-of-goods vs. operating expense
Check for one-off cost items in the period
Review segment-level margin disclosures if available

possible_explanations: Inventory is building up because sales are slowing
Demand forecasting has overestimated actual sales
Product may be facing weaker sell-through or obsolescence risk
evidence_to_check: MD&A — commentary on demand, sell-through, or inventory levels
Notes to accounts — inventory write-down or provisioning disclosures
investigation_path: Compare inventory growth rate to sales growth rate
Check for inventory write-downs or provisions in the notes
Review MD&A for demand or channel commentary

possible_explanations: Additional borrowing has increased interest expense relative to earnings
Earnings available to cover interest have not grown in proportion to new debt
evidence_to_check: Notes to accounts — borrowings schedule and interest rate terms
MD&A — commentary on financing activity or capital structure
investigation_path: Check the purpose of the new debt disclosed in notes or MD&A
Compare interest expense growth to EBIT growth
Assess whether the debt increase is linked to a specific investment or acquisition

possible_explanations: Cash increase is funded by new borrowings rather than operating performance
Company may be raising debt for future investment, acquisition, or liquidity buffer purposes
evidence_to_check: Cash flow statement — financing activities section
Notes to accounts — new borrowings and their stated purpose
investigation_path: Check whether the cash increase is matched by a financing inflow in the cash flow statement
Review MD&A for the stated purpose of new borrowings
Distinguish operating-driven cash build-up from debt-driven cash build-up

possible_explanations: ROE improvement may be driven by increased financial leverage rather than operating performance
Capital structure changes (e.g. buybacks, higher debt) may be inflating ROE relative to ROCE
evidence_to_check: Notes to accounts — capital structure and debt-to-equity disclosures
MD&A — commentary on buybacks or capital allocation
investigation_path: Compare leverage (debt-to-equity) trend alongside ROE and ROCE
Check for share buybacks reducing the equity base
Assess whether ROCE (which is capital-structure-neutral) tells a different story than ROE

possible_explanations: New capital expenditure is beginning to generate depreciation charges as assets are capitalized
This is an expected mechanical relationship as fixed assets grow
evidence_to_check: Notes to accounts — fixed asset schedule and capitalization dates
MD&A — commentary on capacity expansion or capital projects
investigation_path: Check the fixed asset schedule for newly capitalized assets
Verify depreciation policy and useful-life assumptions applied
Confirm the capex is linked to a disclosed expansion or project
